title: The scaffolded brief invites the integer gate the playbook forbids
foundBy: session agent, from a fresh-agent test: an agent that had read the playbook wrote coverage thresholds into three of the four briefs it authored

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestScaffoldPromptsDoNotInventVocabulary -count=1: PASS. Proved by mutation: putting `Met` back into the mission stub fails it by name. End to end, init's closing output now names the playbook, and MANUAL's sample of that output matches the binary, which SURF-303 checks. make check exit 0.

resolution: The scaffolded brief asks for what an author could check rather than what they could count. One worked contrast carries it. An endpoint test that fails without the change holds up, and a coverage percentage invites a member to manufacture coverage. The orchestrator stub carries the other half, that a teammate's reported number is confirmed rather than taken. Neither comment argues the case, because `cs-campaign playbook` now carries the reasoning and every stub points at it.
details:
`init` writes a brief stub that suggests a benchmark and warns about nothing, so an author fills it with the gate the playbook exists to prevent.

The stub's comment under "Proof your work must carry" tells the author to add what this campaign requires, offering a test run, a benchmark or a migration applied. It says nothing about the shape a check should take.

PLAYBOOK says the opposite at length. Verify every number and gate on none. State a count as a property rather than an integer, because an integer pass condition invites a member to manufacture whatever is counted. An unsatisfiable gate is not survivable, because a capable agent finds a way to appear to pass it.

The scaffolding wins that argument. In a fresh-agent test, an agent read the playbook as its second command. It then wrote coverage thresholds into three of four briefs, including a percentage of API coverage and a minimum count of end-to-end journeys. It copied the stub's shape rather than the document's advice.

This is the shape SAC-006 recorded. What the scaffolding shows is what an operator copies, and what it omits is invented. The stub is read at the moment the advice is needed, and the playbook is read before or not at all.

notes.text: Superseded in part by SAC-022. The comments this record improved are gone, because the stubs that carried them are gone. What survives is the guidance itself, now in the playbook under the headings a brief uses.
